Un plan de medios moderno requiere una medición moderna Las audiencias de los creadores de contenido se mueven a gran velocidad y se comportan de forma diferente según la plataforma y el contexto. Estas dinámicas pueden ser difíciles de predecir, pero sí es posible medirlas. Para las marcas que se involucran en grandes acontecimientos como el Mundial de la FIFA, contar con una visión cross-platform global que incluya a los creadores es clave para entender e identificar dónde están las audiencias y qué impacto generan. La economía de los creadores de contenido ya no es un complemento dentro de las estrategias de comunicación, es un componente estructural más del mix de medios y entender su impacto es fundamental para tomar mejores decisiones. title: AI vs. Human Tutor for Language Speaking Practice (July 2026)
summary: July 2026 guide: AI tutor vs. human tutor for language speaking practice. Compare costs, error correction depth, and strategies to build real
body_text: Most comparisons of AI tutors and human tutors treat them like competing products, but they're stronger on completely different axes. If daily reps are what you're missing, one answer makes sense. If you've got a fossilized grammar habit nobody has ever caught, you need the other. This breaks down exactly where each one pulls its weight. TLDR: Swain's Output Hypothesis (1985) explains why speaking practice builds fluency where reading and listening cannot: producing language forces you to notice gaps that comprehension alone never surfaces. Human tutors catch fossilized errors and read cultural register accurately; a 2024 systematic review found roughly 46% of studies pointed to AI chatbots reducing speaking anxiety during interaction. Daily AI sessions run roughly $1.25 per session versus $40 per session for a human tutor at five days a week, making the cost comparison a volume question, not a quality one. The strongest approach pairs four to five short AI sessions weekly for output volume with one human session every one to two weeks for deep error diagnosis. ISSEN is a real-time AI voice tutor on iOS, Android, and web that covers 60+ languages at $20 to $29 USD per month, designed as one input inside a broader study plan, not a replacement for human instruction. What AI tutors can do for language speaking practice Speaking is where most intermediate learners plateau, and the reason is mechanical: recognition trains through reading and listening, but production only develops when you push words out under pressure. Swain's Output Hypothesis (1985) frames this precisely: producing language forces learners to notice gaps that comprehension alone never surfaces. AI voice tutors now cover a specific slice of that mechanism. Here is how AI speaking practice works in practice. What they do today: Hold real-time voice conversation without push-to-talk, so you respond at conversational pace. Calibrate vocabulary, sentence complexity, and speed to your level within a single turn. Stay on-demand across web, iOS, and Android, so a session can start in under a minute at 6 a.m. or 11 p.m. Correct grammar and word choice inline, then loop the corrected form back into the next exchange. None of this is new pedagogy. Pimsleur ran spaced spoken drills on cassette in the 1960s; the friction that has changed is access, not principle. That is also why your language routine needs speaking practice built into it daily. Where human tutors still have the edge A human tutor watches your face when you stumble and adjusts before you ask. That kind of read matters more than it sounds. If you are weighing your options, a comparison of the best AI voice tutors for language learning can help frame the trade-offs. Four things a good human still does better than any AI: Reads emotional state in real time and switches gears when frustration builds, not solely when confidence drops. Explains the pragmatic layer around a phrase: when it lands as friendly, when it lands as rude, why your Berlin colleague went quiet after you used it. Untangles compounding errors that stack across a paragraph, tracing them back to a single grammar habit instead of patching each surface mistake. Holds you accountable through scheduled sessions with someone who remembers what you promised last week. For learners preparing for oral exams, high-stakes interviews, or professional settings with dense cultural coding, a weekly hour with a human on Preply or italki does work an AI session cannot. The limitations of AI tutors for language speaking practice Being clear-eyed about the ceiling matters more than defending the tool. Four weaknesses worth knowing before you build a routine around AI language tutors for conversation practice : Fossilized errors slip through. If you have said "I am agree" for eight years, an AI often accepts the meaning and rolls forward. A trained teacher catches the pattern on the third occurrence and interrupts. Fluency gets rewarded over accuracy. The tutor is optimized to keep you talking, which builds confidence but can quietly reinforce approximations a human would flag. Pragmatic and cultural texture is thin. An AI can define keigo or explain the tu/vous split, but rarely reads the room the way a native colleague does when your register lands wrong. The social stakes are absent. Nothing embarrassing happens when you fumble at 11 p.m. in your kitchen, and embarrassment is part of what glues corrections into long-term memory. Cost and availability: the real trade-off The math changes once you count sessions instead of months. Human tutors in the US typically run $25 to $80 per hour , and scheduling caps how often you can book. AI voice tutors charge a flat monthly rate with unlimited sessions, which changes what you get per dollar when your goal is daily reps. Here is how it looks if you want speaking practice five days a week: Option Monthly cost Sessions Cost per session Human tutor at $40/hr, 1x per week $160 4 $40 Human tutor at $40/hr, 5x per week $800 20 $40 AI voice tutor, flat rate ~$25 20+ ~$1.25 Human tutors are not overpriced. Their unit of value is the session itself: an hour of expert diagnosis. AI tutors sell the opposite unit, which is volume of unstructured spoken output. If you need one, the other stops being a substitute. How speaking anxiety shapes the choice For many adult learners, the barrier to speaking practice is not scheduling or cost. The real obstacle is the freeze that arrives the moment a human is on the other end of the line. That freeze compounds. Skip enough sessions and you stop booking them, which turns anxiety into an access problem, not merely a feelings one. For learners who freeze before human conversation, fear of speaking a foreign language is its own obstacle worth tackling directly. The research on AI chatbots for speaking practice tracks this closely. A 2024 systematic review found that roughly 46% of studies reviewed pointed to chatbots easing speaking anxiety during interaction. What that means in practice: An anxious learner who books zero human sessions gets zero reps. The same learner opening one of the top AI apps for real conversations at 11 p.m. gets 20 minutes of real output. Confidence built against a machine transfers imperfectly to humans, but imperfectly is a long way from nothing. The friction of starting matters more than the quality of any single session. A tutor you actually talk to beats a better tutor you keep postponing. AI tutor vs. human tutor for speaking: a direct comparison Set the two options next to each other on the dimensions that govern speaking progress, and the picture gets clearer. Neither wins outright; each is stronger on a different axis, a pattern worth understanding given how AI language tutoring is changing fluency for many learners. Dimension AI voice tutor Human tutor Real-time feedback Inline, every turn, without emotional read Fewer corrections per hour, calibrated to your state Personalization Adapts vocabulary, pace, and topic mid-turn Builds a long arc across weeks Scheduling On-demand, any hour, any device Booked slots, time-zone friction Cultural accuracy Explains rules; weaker at reading the room Native intuition for register and tone Error correction High volume, surface-level, can miss fossilized habits Lower volume, deeper diagnosis of recurring patterns Cost per session Roughly $1 to $2 at daily use $25 to $80, flat Read the row your goal lives in first. If daily volume matters most, one column answers; if diagnosis matters most, the other does. How to combine AI and human tutors for speaking practice The two modes fix different constraints, so the smart play is to run them in parallel, and solo language speaking practice fills the gaps between scheduled human sessions. Treat AI as the daily practice layer and a human as the periodic correction layer. A workable weekly shape: Four or five short AI sessions (15 to 25 minutes each) for output volume, topic reps, and low-stakes recovery from stumbles. One human session every one to two weeks for structured diagnosis: fossilized errors, register drift, pronunciation habits that need a trained ear. Bring a specific artifact to the human hour. A phrase you kept fumbling with the AI, a recording of yourself, a topic your tutor flagged. Between human sessions, treat the AI as an AI language friend and tutor alternative and drill the corrections until the new form stops feeling deliberate. The human catches what the AI misses. The AI supplies the reps a weekly hour cannot. ISSEN: your on-demand AI voice tutor for real conversation practice If daily reps are the constraint a weekly human hour cannot fix, ISSEN fills exactly that layer. ISSEN is a real-time AI voice tutor on iOS, Android, and web, supporting 60+ languages, with sessions starting within 30 seconds of opening the app. Treat it as one input inside a broader study plan, alongside the best language learning apps for speaking , and not a replacement for grammar work or human conversation. A few things worth knowing before you try it: Smart turn detection means no push-to-talk. The tutor waits when you hesitate and responds when you finish, closer to a phone call than a walkie-talkie. Multilingual support lets you drop into Spanglish mid-sentence without breaking the exchange. Vocabulary, pace, and topic adapt within a single turn, so an A2 session and a B2 session feel structurally different. Pricing runs $20 to $29 USD per month with a 10-minute free trial. Try ISSEN free for 10 minutes. Final thoughts on the AI tutor vs. human tutor question for speaking The constraint stopping you from getting more speaking reps this week is the real question worth answering. If scheduling or cost is the blocker, an AI voice tutor solves that directly. If fossilized errors and cultural register are the issue, a human tutor on italki or Preply is the right call. Most learners benefit from both, and running them together costs less than five human sessions a month. Consider where this is heading for someone like Amara, a supply chain coordinator in Nairobi who needs polished business English for a new regional role in the next six months. Today she is booking one Preply session a week and pushing herself through the awkward pauses. In two years, her ISSEN tutor will already know that she presents to the Nairobi office on Thursdays, that her recurring stumble is hedging language in disagreements, and that last Tuesday's session surfaced three phrases she never finished drilling. The human tutor stays for the diagnosis. The AI fills every gap between those sessions: before the Thursday presentation, after the meeting that went sideways, at 6 a.m. when there is no one else to practice with. The principle behind this has been proven for decades; the friction of access is what's being removed. Start a 10-minute conversation with ISSEN to see what the daily practice layer feels like. FAQ Should I use an AI voice tutor like ISSEN or a human tutor on Preply or italki for daily speaking practice? The answer depends on what you need most: volume or diagnosis. ISSEN gives you unlimited on-demand sessions at roughly $1 to $2 per rep, which makes daily practice financially realistic. Preply and italki tutors charge $25 to $80 per hour and work best as a periodic correction layer, catching fossilized errors and register problems that accumulate between sessions. Can an AI tutor catch fossilized grammar errors the way a human tutor would? Generally, no. AI voice tutors are optimized to keep conversation moving, which builds output volume but can let entrenched errors like "I am agree" pass without targeted interruption. A trained human tutor catches the pattern across multiple occurrences and stops to correct the underlying habit, which is the stronger intervention for errors you have been making for years. How does speaking anxiety affect whether an AI tutor or human tutor is the right choice? If anxiety is causing you to cancel or postpone sessions entirely, an AI tutor removes the social stakes that trigger the freeze response. A 2024 systematic review found that roughly 46% of studies reviewed pointed to AI chatbots easing speaking anxiety during interaction, and any reps completed at 11 p.m. in your kitchen beat zero reps with a better tutor you keep putting off booking. What does an AI language tutor actually do during a speaking session? A purpose-built AI voice tutor like ISSEN drives the conversation instead of waiting for you to prompt it, adjusts vocabulary and speaking pace within a single turn based on your level, corrects grammar inline, and loops corrected forms back into the exchange. That is meaningfully different from opening ChatGPT and asking it to practice Spanish with you, which has no lesson structure, no difficulty calibration, and no memory of what you struggled with last time. How should I combine AI speaking practice with human tutoring for the fastest progress? Run them as two separate layers with distinct jobs. Four or five short AI sessions per week (15 to 25 minutes each) build the output volume a weekly hour cannot supply. One human session every one to two weeks handles structured diagnosis: fossilized errors, register drift, and pronunciation habits that need a trained ear. Bring something specific to that human session, a phrase you kept fumbling or a recording of yourself, then drill the corrections against the AI until the corrected form stops feeling deliberate.

title: The Burnham era begins
summary: What could the new UK prime minister mean for fiscal policy, economic growth and financial markets? Discover what investors should know.
body_text: The Burnham era begins UK POLITICS 20 July 2026 Luke Mayberry, Investment Strategist Share this Insight Share page via Facebook Share page via X Share page via LinkedIn Share page via email Andy Burnham MP has been appointed prime minister, bringing months of uncertainty to an end. Following Sir Keir Starmer's resignation, Burnham was unopposed in the race for the Labour leadership, with no candidate formally mounting a challenge against him. With the political transition complete, investor attention now turns to policy and what it could mean for markets. Policy agenda Burnham has pledged to pursue a regionally focused growth agenda centred on housing, infrastructure, devolution and skills. His first major policy speech placed devolved decision-making at its core, shifting funding and powers away from Whitehall towards mayors and local authorities, to be done through a new Manchester-based operation he has dubbed "Number 10 North". On housing, he has committed to the largest council housebuilding programme since the post-war period. He has also proposed business rates reform aimed at supporting the high streets. His broader growth agenda points towards regional industrial strategy and a stronger technical and vocational skills offer. Tax policy is the biggest area of uncertainty. Speculation has centred on potential reforms to property and wealth taxation, including Burnham's previously expressed interest in a land value tax, alongside possible changes to inheritance tax and council tax. However, no proposals have been confirmed, and the political and practical hurdles to major reform remain considerable. What should investors watch? Several developments will be important for investors in the coming months, but the Autumn Budget is likely to be the most significant. It will provide the first detailed insight into how the government intends to balance its growth ambitions with fiscal discipline. Any changes to taxation are most likely to be announced at this point, while the accompanying fiscal forecasts will reveal how much room the chancellor has to manoeuvre. Until then, investors should focus on formal policy announcements rather than political speculation. While headlines and rumours are likely to fuel uncertainty in the months ahead, individuals should be cautious about making impulsive, short-term decisions relating to their wealth and investments based on unconfirmed policy changes. The run-up to the first Budget will be just as important. Investors will be paying close attention to signals from the Treasury as Chancellor John Healey begins to set out his economic agenda. His appointment came as a surprise to many and leaves markets with relatively little insight into how he will balance the government's growth ambitions with the need to maintain fiscal credibility. Speeches, interviews and Labour's party conference in late September may provide important clues about the direction of tax and spending policy before the Budget itself. Market implications Financial markets have already begun adjusting to the new political landscape. Gilts and sterling have rallied as the shape of the new government became clearer, a notable contrast to the spring when Burnham's emergence as the frontrunner for the Labour leadership prompted concerns over higher borrowing and a looser fiscal stance. That said, investor confidence will ultimately depend on whether the government's fiscal discipline matches its policy ambitions. As a result, volatility is likely to remain elevated in the weeks ahead and any politically-driven rise in gilt yields could present an attractive opportunity for investors looking to add exposure. For equities, the impact is likely to vary considerably. The FTSE 100 remains relatively insulated, with around three-quarters of its revenues generated overseas, while the FTSE 250's greater domestic exposure means it is likely to be more influenced by developments in fiscal, housing and regional growth policy. At the sector level, construction and housebuilding stand to benefit most directly if the council housing pledge progresses with funding behind it, while regional infrastructure could be a secondary beneficiary of the devolution agenda. Areas facing greater uncertainty include utilities, where investors will be watching closely for any signs of tighter regulation or increased public-sector involvement. For the Bank of England, the fiscal backdrop adds another layer of uncertainty to the rates outlook. With markets already pricing in hikes through year-end, a credible Autumn Budget could ease that pressure, while any fiscal slippage risks keeping rates higher for longer. The bottom line Political uncertainty has largely given way to policy uncertainty. But until the Autumn Budget, tax speculation is just noise that should be ignored. Instead, investors’ focus should be, in our view, on sector-specific opportunities within equities and on taking advantage of any politically driven entry points in gilt markets. title: What personal health strategies can teach us about utility asset health (part 1)
summary: Studies on corporate wellness programs have shown that companies that proactively focus on improving employee health and well-being see significant benefits including a reduction in lost work days and employee healthcare costs. One of the key drivers of success for wellness programs is the proactive nature of monitoring and managing lifestyle factors such as nutrition and fitness.
body_text: Studies on corporate wellness programs have shown that companies that proactively focus on improving employee health and well-being see significant benefits including a reduction in lost work days and employee healthcare costs. One of the key drivers of success for wellness programs is the proactive nature of monitoring and managing lifestyle factors such as nutrition and fitness. Just like personal health, a utility’s assets―from power cables and substations to pipelines―need to be actively monitored and maintained in order to continue to operate at peak performance. The same holds true for other asset-intensive industries such as oil and gas and transportation. A healthy asset management strategy requires a proactive and strategic approach to meet your business needs today and lays the groundwork for long-term viability. Is your asset management strategy “fit” for the future? Whether we’re talking about personal health or the health of your business, one thing rings true – consistency is key. Improving your overall health takes preparation and commitment. Similarly, strengthening and managing your business assets requires a clear and consistent strategy. To remain competitive, utilities and other asset-intensive industries should assess and advance the maturity of their asset management program along the following dimensions: Take action │Harness asset data As healthy food fuels the body, data is the fuel required for a healthy asset management strategy. Advanced technology through smart devices, supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems and the adoption of IoT-based solutions means that more data is available than ever before. But remember data is only useful if it can be transformed into actionable insights that drive business performance and results. Put your data to work! Taking the first step │Develop a solid baseline of current performance of assets You need to have clear visibility and understanding of the overall current health of your assets. Every personal health program starts with a baseline assessment, whether it’s your first weigh-in or initial evaluation with a personal trainer. The baseline must include an evaluation of how long a current asset can be maintained, and when it will need to be replaced. However, there are other variables to take into account too. Asset degradation, for instance, will vary from one location to another. An overhead power line that is in use in a coastal area may be subject to salt erosion, while same line in a hot, arid climate may suffer heat damage. Once this baseline is established, you can better develop a strategic plan for how to meet expected future performance needs. The “heart” of the matter │Understand the criticality of assets A healthy asset management program must include cost-effective intervention and replacement plans for critical assets. Organizations must strike a balance between containing costs, while still continuing to deliver quality service. To do so, they must understand the consequence of asset failure in terms of impact to financial, safety, environmental and service quality business objectives. Spending money on maintaining and replacing assets which do not make a significant difference to operational performance may be an unwise business decision. Avoid the quick fix │Manage the total asset budget For asset-intensive industries, short-term tradeoffs are often made between capital expenditures (CapEx) and operational expenditures (OpEx). Making short-term asset decisions to reduce either CapEx or OpEx spend independently might jeopardize the overall health of your assets in the long-term. It is necessary to ensure a balance between both CapEx and OpEx, and focus on the overall value of each asset to the organization. It’s a lifestyle change │Take an enterprise view of asset management Evolving your asset management strategy will require utilities and other asset-intensive industries to integrate asset management across the entire enterprise. This requires adopting new ways of working collaboratively across the organization, such as breaking down organizational silos to integrate various data sources (operational, IT, financial, GIS, etc.) into one platform. However it enables a deeper analysis and better overall asset management performance. I invite you to read more on this topic in our white paper on Active Asset Management: Enabling utilities to gain a competitive edge.

title: Automated Sales-to-CS Handovers: Onboarding That Starts With Full Context
summary: Most churn risk starts at the sales-to-CS handover. How automated handovers move goals, promises, and stakeholder context into onboarding, without a rep writing a summary.
body_text: TL;DR The sales-to-CS handover is where deals quietly start to churn: goals, promises, and stakeholder context live in the closing rep's head, and Customer Success starts from scratch. Automated handovers fix this structurally. An AI sales agent extracts commitments, stakeholders, and objections from the actual sales calls and delivers them to CS through the CRM or Slack, the moment the deal closes. Why handovers fail even on good teams The deal closes, the champagne pops, and the most valuable knowledge in the account is about to evaporate. Sales knows everything at that moment: the customer's real goals, the promises made, which feature sealed the deal, which objection almost killed it. But that knowledge lives in scattered notes, unwatched recordings, and the rep's memory. So CS opens the relationship with a discovery call, and the customer explains everything again, to the second person from the same company in three weeks. This isn't an effort problem. Reps are racing to the next deal, CSMs are juggling a dozen onboardings, and the handover meeting gets compressed into a Slack message. Manual handovers don't scale, and the customer can tell when CS is improvising instead of executing on what was promised. We see the damage in our own customer conversations. Before OMR Reviews automated their handovers with Demodesk, tracking what sales had promised was a source of friction between the sales and CS teams. Tanso named handover quality as one of the three problems they bought us to fix. What an automated handover contains The fix isn't a better handover template. It's removing the human bottleneck between the sales conversations and the CS team. When a sales call ends, the AI Assistant analyzes the recording and extracts the parts that matter for the next owner of the account: Customer goals and pain points , in the customer's own words Stakeholders and roles : who decided, who evaluated, who blocked Commitments : deliverables, timelines, and promises made by sales Features discussed and why they mattered to this specific buyer Objections raised and how they were resolved , with timestamps into the recording The critical property: this comes from the transcript, not from what the rep remembers at 6 pm on closing day. Promises that were made get documented. Promises that weren't made can't be invented. How it reaches the CS team The extraction is only half the handover. Delivery has two paths, and most teams use both. Through the CRM. Demodesk writes the handover data into Salesforce, HubSpot, or Pipedrive as notes, tasks, and field updates, including custom fields like “integration complexity” or “champion confidence”, with 99% accuracy and approval before push. Your CRM's existing automation takes over from there: task assignment, onboarding stage triggers, dashboards. The CRM stays the single source of truth. Through notifications. The moment analysis completes, CS gets the handover summary in Slack, Teams, or email: goals, commitments, stakeholder map, and direct links to the timestamped moments in the recording. No logging into a new tool, no waiting for the weekly handover meeting. What the handover looks like in practice A closed deal produces a summary like this, without anyone writing it: Handover: Acme Corp Primary goal: reduce new-hire onboarding time by 30% Stakeholders: Jane Doe (HR Director, decision maker, budget owner) · John Smith (IT Lead, ran technical evaluation, owns integration concerns) Commitments made: custom HRIS integration by Q2 · dedicated onboarding session with an integration specialist · bi-weekly check-ins for the first 60 days Critical context: main objection was integration complexity with legacy systems, resolved via API walkthrough (recording, minute 42). Faster implementation than the competing vendor was the deciding factor. Next actions: schedule integration kickoff with John within 5 days · prepare HRIS integration proposal · introduce Jane to her CSM The difference shows on the first CS call. Instead of “tell me about your goals,” the CSM opens with “you're aiming for 30% faster onboarding, and John had concerns about the legacy HRIS, so let's start with the integration kickoff.” The customer feels continuity instead of a restart. Once the handover works, the same records power the reverse direction too: renewal and expansion conversations where CS hands context back to sales. Results worth expecting Ignore vendors who promise a churn percentage from better handovers; too many variables sit between a summary and a renewal. What automated handovers verifiably change: The handover exists for every deal. No exceptions for busy weeks, because no one has to write it. Commitments become auditable. “They told us X” disputes end with a timestamped recording link. CS time shifts from gathering to delivering. OMR Reviews reports less conflict between sales and CS and 3+ hours saved per rep per week since Demodesk became their single source of truth for sales conversations. Onboarding starts within hours, not weeks , because there's no discovery call to schedule first.

title: Rose Rocket + Alpine Logistics: Cutting Invoicing from Weeks to 48 Hours
summary: Customer Story: Alpine Logistics
body_text: Alpine Logistics is a family-owned business specializing in automotive expedite shipments. Founded by Rod Rice, who spent 20 years managing logistics for Honda, the company is built on long-standing customer relationships and deep industry experience. His son, Aaron Rice, grew up in the business, helping with paperwork from a young age and now leading backend operations as Office Manager. With five employees and five trucks (a mix of cargo vans and 26ft box trucks), Alpine is known for reliability and speed. Eventually, the company reached a point where relying on paper and spreadsheets could no longer keep up. The Challenge: Surviving on Spreadsheets and Paperwork For years, Alpine ran operations on Excel and Google Sheets. Orders were entered by hand, drivers turned in paperwork at the end of the day, and invoices were created in QuickBooks after multiple rounds of re-typing the same information. To keep track of order numbers across documents, the team also relied on a whiteboard system in the office. Numbers were written on the board for visibility, then copied into Excel, printed on paperwork, and later re-entered into QuickBooks. This patchwork process worked, until it didn’t. During busy periods, it led to missed trips, duplicate orders, and stacks of unassigned paperwork that delayed invoicing for weeks. “We reached the point where the existing process was holding us back. I’d be running operations in the morning and driving a truck in the afternoon, all while chasing down paperwork. It wasn’t sustainable.” - Aaron Rice, Office Manager, Alpine Logistics Why Alpine Chose Rose Rocket When evaluating TMS solutions, Alpine needed something powerful but easy to run alongside a small team. Other vendors required hours of training and shutting down operations for two weeks. For a five-truck company, that simply was not possible. Rose Rocket stood out because it offered: Affordable growth: A solution that fit the budget of a small carrier but could scale with the business. Easy to use: An intuitive system that drivers and staff could pick up right away. Fast to implement: Rose Rocket was running alongside operations without downtime. Trusted partnership: Years of conversations with Rose Rocket ’s team gave Aaron confidence in the decision. “I wish I jumped on it sooner than I did,” Aaron admitted. “It felt like an expense at the time, but it’s more than paid for itself.” The Results with Rose Rocket By moving onto Rose Rocket, Alpine replaced re-typing and paperwork with one connected system: Invoicing speed: Cut from 1–2 weeks to just 48 hours Error prevention: Orders cannot close without required paperwork, eliminating missed documents No more duplicates: Automated checks keep the operation clean Faster order entry: Order numbers auto-assigned, data added quickly with AI-driven workflows One platform: Replaced spreadsheets, and QuickBooks hand-offs Alpine is also piloting TED, Rose Rocket’s AI-powered inbox assistant. “The email-to-order automation is the most valuable feature we’re testing right now. It means orders just flow into the system without me touching them.” Everyday Impact Today, Aaron manages operations primarily through Rose Rocket, while drivers use the mobile app for dispatch and paperwork. Rod occasionally logs in to monitor activity, but the entire team benefits from having one connected platform. Customer support has also been a highlight. “Anytime I have a question, I get an immediate response. That makes a big difference when you’re running lean like we are.” Looking Forward Alpine is navigating a tough freight market with confidence, thanks to Rose Rocket. What started as a family business running on whiteboards and spreadsheets is now a technology-enabled operation built for resilience and growth. “For a small company, Rose Rocket has been the perfect fit. It gave us the tools we needed to survive, and now it’s helping us plan for the future.” - Aaron Rice, Office Manager, Alpine Logistics

title: 5 recommendations to improve the customer agent experience
summary: This CGI blog post five recommendations to improve the customer agent experience.
body_text: Today, the customer experience is of paramount importance. Once again, through the CGI Voice of Our Clients insights , we find that becoming digital to satisfy the needs of customers and citizens is the number one trend across industries, and the customer and citizen experience is a top business and technology priority for most. Contact centers are increasingly becoming an integral part of the customer journey. Organizations are striving to provide a superior customer experience to differentiate themselves. As the customer experience moves to the forefront of their business priorities, the importance of the customer service agent correspondingly increases. To satisfy customers, customer service agents should be equipped to provide exceptional service. However, too often, customer service agents and contact centers are undervalued and insufficiently equipped. In this blog, we explore why and how organizations should be investing in their customer service agents. Overall, customer and employee experiences should converge to create a coherent delivery approach that drives business outcomes. Undervalued and insufficiently equipped agents Historically, organizations have viewed customer contact centers as essential yet non-strategic cost centers, and many still hold that view today. Often organizations perceive agents as low-value workers, even though agents are arguably doing the most valuable work of an organization (i.e., directly interfacing with customers). They have a huge impact on customer satisfaction and retention. Customer service agents earn relatively modest pay and receive fewer benefits, such as the option to work from home and flexible hours, than other workers receive. Agents clock in and out, take scheduled breaks, and work under close supervision. Technology wise, contact centers often operate using multiple, non-integrated legacy systems. When answering customer queries, an agent may need to consult several systems at a time to find the right information, and inconsistencies in system data can require the agent to consult the back office to get the correct information. While artificial intelligence (AI) solutions exist to remedy these challenges, agent work environments are frequently under-invested and lag behind the rest of the organization they serve. The impact of a poor agent experience These conditions result in traditional and regimented work environments, low job satisfaction, and little opportunity for career growth, which, in turn, lead to high agent turnover. With high agent turnover, organizations incur significant costs related to onboarding and training new agents, as well as knowledge loss, all of which affect the entire organization, including the customer experience. The bottom line is clear; it is impossible to deliver excellent customer service if you provide a poor agent experience. Leading organizations understand this and, in turn, equip, motivate and support their agents through a rich and rewarding work experience. They value agents beyond basic performance metrics, viewing them and treating them as strategic to their business. Best practices for creating a superior agent experience How are leading organizations creating a rich and rewarding experience for agents? Here are just a few best practices they follow: Take care of your agents, just as you do your customers. Value them. Provide them with the same benefits other workers receive, such as the option to work from home, flexible hours and autonomy. The best contact centers use a workforce management app that places control of working conditions into the hands of the agent. Entrust agents with high-value tasks. Separate low-value transactions from high-value transactions based on the customer experience, and entrust your agents with high-value tasks. Consider debt recovery services as an example. Accessing an account balance is a low-value transaction prime for automation, while negotiating a payment plan is a more high-value service, requiring the human understanding and empathy of an agent. Empower agents to converse with customers, rather than use a regimented script, and reward them for successfully handling high-value transactions. Automate low-value tasks and equip agents with performance-enhancing tools and technologies. If you provide virtual assistant tools like chatbots for your customers, provide the same for your agents. Use technology to enhance the agent experience in the same way you use it to enhance the customer experience. AI is a key technology for creating a supportive agent work experience. Agents can use AI to search databases, navigate applications and update multiple systems at one time, freeing them up to concentrate more on the customer experience. Invest in continuous agent training and career growth. Traditional training involves classrooms and materials. Invest in modern training in which you use technology to provide agents with feedback and coaching in real time based on their real-time customer interactions. Use AI, for example, to monitor customer calls in real time, anticipate agent needs, provide data, and offer coaching. In addition, provide not only initial onboarding training, but also ongoing programs required for upskilling and reskilling. Create opportunities for your agents to develop their knowledge and skills and pursue a career path. Changing the culture, tools and processes of a contact center to create a superior agent experience requires the right interventions at the right time. To manage all of the necessary changes for agents, as well as equip leadership to rollout and support change, choose a partner with in-depth experience in building innovative, high-performance, outcome-based contact centers. CGI’s unique offerings in change management, smart business operations, and human-centered design can help you get started. Contact Peter Skelton at CGI to learn how CGI can support your organization in this work.

title: UroGen Receives New U.S. Patent Allowance Expected to Provide Protection into July 2044 for ZUSDURI™ and UGN-103
summary: PRINCETON, N.J., July 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- UroGen Pharma Ltd. (Nasdaq: URGN), a biotech company dedicated to developing and commercializing innovative solutions that treat urothelial and specialty cancers, today announced that it has received a Notice of Allowance from the U.S.
body_text: PRINCETON, N.J., July 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- UroGen Pharma Ltd. (Nasdaq: URGN), a biotech company dedicated to developing and commercializing innovative solutions that treat urothelial and specialty cancers, today announced that it has received a Notice of Allowance from the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) for patent application no. 18/784,354 entitled “Treatment of Low-Grade Intermediate-Risk Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer With a Thermally Gelling Pharmaceutical Composition Containing Mitomycin.” The allowed claims cover methods of treating patients with recurrent, low-grade intermediate-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (LG-IR-NMIBC) without a transurethral resection of a bladder tumor (TURBT), supported by data from the ENVISION and ATLAS clinical trials. The U.S. patent, once issued, will have an expiration date in July 2044. “This patent allowance further strengthens the intellectual property foundation supporting ZUSDURI and our UGN-103 investigational medicine, if approved, and underscores the innovation behind our proprietary RTGel ® technology,” said Liz Barrett, President and Chief Executive Officer of UroGen. “Supported by data from the ENVISION and ATLAS trials of ZUSDURI, these patent claims reflect the ability of our RTGel -based technology to deliver mitomycin as a primary, non-surgical treatment option for adults with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC without a TURBT. We believe this approach helps patients achieve highly durable recurrence-free intervals while reducing the burden of repeat surgical interventions.” Building on the growing body of clinical evidence supporting ZUSDURI and UGN-103, UroGen remains focused on advancing its proprietary RTGel technology and developing innovative therapies that have the potential to expand non-surgical treatment options for patients with urothelial cancers and strengthen the company’s long-term growth opportunities. About ZUSDURI ZUSDURI (mitomycin) for intravesical solution is an innovative drug formulation of mitomycin, approved for the treatment of adults with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. Utilizing UroGen’s proprietary RTGel technology (a sustained release, hydrogel-based formulation), ZUSDURI is delivered directly into the bladder by a trained healthcare professional using a urinary catheter in an outpatient setting, thereby enabling the treatment of tumors by non-surgical means. About UGN-103 In January 2024, UroGen entered into a licensing and supply agreement with medac to develop UGN-103 for recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. UGN-103 is designed to reinforce and extend the clinical and commercial profile of ZUSDURI, the first and only FDA-approved treatment for adults with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC. The program maintains UroGen’s innovative and proven RTGel technology, enabling sustained mitomycin exposure in the bladder, while incorporating next-generation enhancements, including a more streamlined manufacturing process and simplified reconstitution to support improved ease of use in clinical practice. UroGen holds U.S. patents covering the combination of its proprietary RTGel technology with medac’s licensed lyophilized mitomycin formulation, as well as the use of UGN-103 in LG-IR-NMIBC, with intellectual property protection expected to extend into December 2041. About UroGen Pharma Ltd. UroGen is a biotech company dedicated to developing and commercializing innovative solutions that treat urothelial and specialty cancers because patients deserve better options. UroGen has developed RTGel reverse-thermal hydrogel, a proprietary sustained-release, hydrogel-based platform technology that has the potential to improve the therapeutic profiles of existing drugs. UroGen’s sustained release technology is designed to enable longer exposure of the urinary tract tissue to medications, making local therapy a potentially more effective treatment option. Our first product to treat low-grade upper tract urothelial cancer and our second product, ZUSDURI (mitomycin) for intravesical solution for adult patients with recurrent LG-IR-NMIBC, are designed to ablate tumors by non-surgical means. UroGen is headquartered in Princeton, NJ with operations in Israel. Visit www.UroGen.com to learn more or follow us on X (formerly Twitter), @UroGenPharma. About medac At medac group, we believe that health is humanity’s most valuable resource. Since 1970, our mission has been to improve patients’ quality of life worldwide by making the best medical treatments available. As a globally operating pharmaceutical company headquartered in Germany, we provide high-quality medical treatments for patients worldwide in over 90 countries. With more than 2,000 employees, we are committed to improving human health. Our products are manufactured in Germany and other European countries to the highest standards, utilizing our own logistics center and production sites, and subsequently distributed worldwide. We are constantly working to improve authorized medicines and to develop innovative therapies in the fields of rheumatology, urology, hematology, and oncology. Part of our mission is to provide safe, high-quality and innovative original products, as well as generics and biosimilars. In this way, we make vital treatments accessible to those affected. For more information, please visit www.medac-group.com. APPROVED USE FOR ZUSDURI ZUSDURI (mitomycin) for intravesical solution is a prescription medicine used to treat adults with a type of cancer of the lining of the bladder called low-grade intermediate risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (LG-IR-NMIBC) after previously receiving bladder surgery to remove tumor that did not work or is no longer working. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION You should not receive ZUSDURI if you have a hole or tear (perforation) of your bladder or if you have had an allergic reaction to mitomycin or to any of the ingredients in ZUSDURI. Before receiving ZUSDURI, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you: have kidney problems are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. ZUSDURI can harm your unborn baby. You should not become pregnant during treatment with ZUSDURI. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you become pregnant or think you may be pregnant during treatment with ZUSDURI. Females who are able to become pregnant: You should use effective birth control (contraception) during treatment with ZUSDURI and for 6 months after the last dose. Males being treated with ZUSDURI: You should use effective birth control (contraception) during treatment with ZUSDURI and for 3 months after the last dose. are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if ZUSDURI passes into your breast milk. Do not breastfeed during treatment with ZUSDURI and for 1 week after the last dose. How will I receive ZUSDURI? You will receive your ZUSDURI dose from your healthcare provider 1 time a week for 6 weeks into your bladder through a tube called a urinary catheter. It is important that you receive all 6 doses of ZUSDURI according to your healthcare provider’s instructions. If you miss any appointments, call your healthcare provider as soon as possible to reschedule your appointment. During treatment with ZUSDURI, your healthcare provider may tell you to take additional medicines or change how you take your current medicines. After receiving ZUSDURI: ZUSDURI may cause your urine color to change to a violet to blue color. Avoid contact between your skin and urine for at least 24 hours. To urinate, males and females should sit on a toilet and flush the toilet several times after you use it. After going to the bathroom, wash your hands, your inner thighs, and genital area well with soap and water. Clothing that comes in contact with urine should be washed right away and washed separately from other clothing. The most common side effects of ZUSDURI include: increased blood creatinine levels, increased blood potassium levels, trouble with urination, decreased red blood cell counts, increase in certain blood liver tests, increased or decreased white blood cell counts, urinary tract infection, and blood in your urine. You are encouraged to report negative side effects of prescription drugs to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/medwatch or call 1-800-FDA-1088. You may also report side effects to UroGen Pharma at 1-855-987-6436. Please see ZUSDURI Full Prescribing Information, including the Patient Information, for additional information. title: How to find new immunology indications with AI and multiomics data
summary: A blockbuster therapy’s patent expiration is often seen as the end of its commercial journey, but it doesn’t have to be. The trick lies in finding new opportunities, which requires […] The post How to find new immunology indications with AI and multiomics data appeared first on Bioinformatics Software | QIAGEN Digital Insights .
body_text: A blockbuster therapy’s patent expiration is often seen as the end of its commercial journey, but it doesn’t have to be. The trick lies in finding new opportunities, which requires a comprehensive understanding of the interactions between drugs, pathways, drugs and biological mechanisms. Discovery scientists are starting to combine curated biological knowledge, multiomics data and AI-supported interpretation to build a more complete understanding of human biology and support indication expansion. Webinar See it in action Get all the details with a demonstration from field application scientists Tim Hou, PhD and Ethan Strattan, PhD (or skip to the recap at 51:39). Watch the replay In action: New opportunities for ustekinumab (Stelara®) Ustekinumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting the IL-12/IL-23 signaling pathway from Janssen, has been approved for plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis. It offers a practical example of how integrated biological knowledge can uncover new therapeutic opportunities. Although the therapy effectively suppresses key inflammatory pathways in psoriasis and other immune-mediated diseases, not all patients achieve a sustained response. Initial non-response, loss of response over time and persistent disease activity suggest that not all inflammatory mechanisms were affected by the treatment. Mapping persistent disease mechanisms Here's one approach for using public datasets1,2 to identify treatment-responsive pathways and mechanisms that remain active despite therapy (Table 1). 01 Which biological pathways respond to ustekinumab treatment? Canonical pathway analysis integrates transcriptomic data with curated biological knowledge to predict pathways that are activated or inhibited by therapy. 02 Which disease mechanisms are active even with treatment? Comparative analysis reveals pathways that persist after IL-12/IL-23 inhibition, highlighting potential mechanisms of treatment resistance. 03 What regulates these persistent pathways? Upstream regulator analysis identifies IL1A, IL1B, IL1R, IL4 and IL17A as potential drivers of residual disease activity and novel therapeutic targets. 04 Which candidates are the most promising? Integrated evidence helps prioritize biomarkers, identify existing drugs targeting these pathways and select appropriate models for validation. While ustekinumab effectively inhibited many inflammatory pathways, several disease-associated pathways remained active, providing a starting point for identifying new therapeutic targets and combination strategies that could improve patient response. After identifying persistent inflammatory pathways and shared upstream regulators, researchers can validate their findings with the curated data in DKB. A workflow that connects evidence to discovery These analyses were made possible with complementary technologies contributing different layers of evidence and interpretation. By bringing together transcriptomic data, pathway analysis, knowledge graphs and AI interpretation, researchers can uncover biomarkers, therapeutic targets and new research directions. QIAGEN Discovery Knowledge Base This knowledge graph incorporates over 200 million curated biological relationships, creating the context needed to interpret findings. title: Shaping UK Sovereign AI: The Lumen Sovereign Public Request for Input is Live
summary: Help shape the future of Britain’s first sovereign frontier AI. Cosine is seeking public input on capabilities, use cases, and governance for Lumen Sovereign, our secure, UK-built model for critical sectors.
body_text: Cosine is building Lumen Sovereign , Britain's first fully sovereign frontier AI for critical sectors. As we shared in our recent landmark coalition announcement , many of the UK's most vital institutions face a difficult reality. The models they depend on are controlled, trained, and operated overseas, creating unacceptable risks to security and sovereignty. We are building Lumen to change that. Backed by the UK Government's £500 million Sovereign AI programme , Lumen Sovereign will be trained entirely on UK soil using Isambard-AI, one of Europe's most powerful supercomputers. Targeted for completion by the end of 2026, it will be fully deployable in air-gapped and high-security environments. We want to hear from you As part of the design phase, we are inviting individuals and industry leaders to contribute their expertise. Our objective is to understand the real-world tasks and workflows that Lumen Sovereign should be able to perform effectively, both as an autonomous agent and through conversational interactions. We want to know: What capabilities and use cases should a sovereign-trained LLM prioritise? Where do current models fall short? What safety, assurance, or governance requirements must be met? Are there specific datasets, benchmarks, or evaluation methods we should use? What tools would the model need to operate effectively in your workflows? And more. By inviting public input, we ensure this capability is built with transparency and aligned with the unique requirements of the society it serves. Your input will help shape Lumen Sovereign's capabilities and support our mission to bring world-class, agentic AI to the UK. Share your input and help shape the future of UK AI .

title: Tenaris expands renewable energy production in Europe with two photovoltaic plants in Italy
summary: Tenaris has completed the installation of two new photovoltaic plants at its Sabbio Bergamasco and Arcore facilities in Italy, further contributing towards Tenaris’s target to reduce CO₂ emissions by 30% by 2030, compared to 2018 levels.
body_text: PUBLISHED ON 07/15/2026 Share Share PUBLISHED ON 07/15/2026 Solar park at Sabbio facility Italy Tenaris has completed the installation of two new photovoltaic plants at its Sabbio Bergamasco and Arcore facilities in Italy, further contributing towards Tenaris’s target to reduce CO₂ emissions by 30% by 2030, compared to 2018 levels. “This project, which includes two photovoltaic plants with a combined peak capacity of 10 MW and an investment of approximately €10 million, is part of a broader roadmap that combines initiatives already implemented with new projects planned for the coming years,” said Michele Della Briotta, President of Tenaris Europe. “Over the next three years, we expect to further expand our renewable energy production in Italy by adding further photovoltaic plants.” The photovoltaic plant in Sabbio Bergamasco has an installed capacity of approximately 5 MW, with 100% of the energy produced expected to be used at our adjacent Dalmine mill. The Arcore plant also has an installed capacity of around 5 MW, with approximately 70% to 75% of the energy produced expected to be self-consumed. Both plants were connected to the national electricity grid in June. The plants were designed with a focus on sustainable land use. In Sabbio Bergamasco, the photovoltaic facility was developed by repurposing an existing storage area, while in Arcore the installation was carried out on rooftops, an approach that could be replicated in future initiatives to make use of existing spaces without additional land consumption. The initiative adds to Tenaris’s investments in renewable energy production in Europe and across its global industrial network. These investments include a solar energy plant at our Silcotub steel mill in Romania, two wind farms in Argentina , and a photovoltaic plant in China . title: Noble Corporation plc Announces First Quarter 2026 Results
summary: HOUSTON, April 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Noble Corporation plc (NYSE: NE, "Noble" or the "Company") today reported first quarter 2026 results.
body_text: Approximately $565 million in new contract value since the January fleet status report, including 3-year extension for the Noble Courage and 5-well contract for the Noble Deliverer ; backlog stands at $7.5 billion. $0.50 per share cash dividend declared for Q2, maintaining consistent return of capital program. Q1 Net Income of $121 million, Diluted Earnings per Share of $0.75, Adjusted Diluted Earnings per Share of $0.26, Adjusted EBITDA of $277 million, net cash provided by operating activities of $273 million, and Free Cash Flow of $169 million. Full Year 2026 Guidance for Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA maintained, 2026 capital expenditures guidance increased by $25 million due to the reactivation of the Noble Deliverer . HOUSTON, April 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Noble Corporation plc (NYSE: NE, “Noble” or the “Company”) today reported first quarter 2026 results. Three Months Ended (in millions, except per share amounts) March 31, 2026 March 31, 2025 December 31, 2025 Total Revenue $ 786 $ 874 $ 764 Contract Drilling Services Revenue 743 832 705 Net Income (Loss) 121 108 87 Adjusted EBITDA* 277 338 232 Adjusted Net Income (Loss)* 41 42 14 Basic Earnings (Loss) Per Share 0.76 0.68 0.55 Diluted Earnings (Loss) Per Share 0.75 0.67 0.54 Adjusted Diluted Earnings (Loss) Per Share* 0.26 0.26 0.09 * A Non-GAAP supporting schedule is included with the statements and schedules in this press release. Robert W. Eifler, President and Chief Executive Officer of Noble, stated, “We commenced 2026 with solid operational and financial results. Commercial momentum remains brisk, highlighted by the Noble Courage’s three year extension with Petrobras and the Noble Deliverer’s five-well program with Woodside. We remain intensely focused on project execution, with several important contract commencements scheduled over the course of this year, each of which is progressing well.” First Quarter Results Contract drilling services revenue for the first quarter of 2026 totaled $743 million compared to $705 million in the prior quarter, with the sequential increase driven primarily by improved fleet utilization. Utilization of the 29 marketed rigs was 68% in the first quarter of 2026 compared to 64% for the same rigs in the prior quarter. Contract drilling services costs for the first quarter were $450 million, down from $471 million in the prior quarter. Net income (loss) increased to $121 million in the first quarter of 2026, up from $87 million in the prior quarter, and Adjusted EBITDA increased to $277 million in the first quarter of 2026, up from $232 million in the prior quarter. Net cash provided by operating activities in the first quarter of 2026 was $273 million, capital expenditures were $104 million, and free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $169 million. Additionally, net disposal proceeds during the quarter totaled $206 million, representing the cash consideration received from the previously announced sale of five jackups to Borr Drilling. Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation The Company’s balance sheet as of March 31, 2026, reflected total debt principal value of $1.9 billion and cash (and cash equivalents) of $663 million. The Company redeemed $55 million principal amount of the 8.5% senior secured notes due 2030 during the first quarter. Additionally, the Company completed the lease buy-out on the first two (of four total) Blackships BOP systems for $36.5 million during the first quarter. The buy-out of the remaining two BOP systems is expected to occur later in 2026 for $36.5 million. In total, the lease buy-out for all four systems is expected to cost $73 million. On April 26, 2026, Noble’s Board of Directors approved an interim quarterly cash dividend on our ordinary shares of $0.50 per share for the second quarter of 2026. The $0.50 per share dividend is expected to be paid on June 25, 2026, to shareholders of record at close of business on June 4, 2026. Future quarterly dividends and other shareholder returns will be subject to, amongst other things, approval by the Board of Directors. Operating Highlights and Backlog Noble’s fleet of 24 marketed floaters was 68% contracted during the first quarter compared with 62% in the prior quarter. Recent contract awards since last quarter have added approximately 5 rig years of new floater backlog. Recent dayrate fixtures for Tier-1 drillships have increased moderately to the low-to-mid $400,000s. Utilization of Noble’s five ultra harsh jackups was 66% in the first quarter versus 72% during the prior quarter. Subsequent to last quarter’s earnings press release, new contracts with a total contract value of approximately $565 million include the following: Noble Courage was extended by Petrobras for an additional 1,115 days, extending through December 2030, for a net incremental backlog addition of $339 million. The dayrate from April 2026 through December 2027 has been reduced from $290,100 to $280,000, followed by the 1,115 days extension at $309,500 per day. Noble Deliverer was awarded a 5-well contract with Woodside in Australia. The contract, valued at $121 million excluding additional services and potential upgrades, is anticipated to commence in Q2 or Q3 2027 and includes options for up to two additional wells. Noble Developer received a one-well contract from ExxonMobil in Guyana at a dayrate of $375,000. This contract is scheduled to commence in early 2027 in direct continuation of the rig’s current program. Noble BlackRhino had an option well exercised by Beacon in the U.S. Gulf which commenced recently in April. Noble Venturer received a one-well contract with Planet One in Ghana, at a dayrate of $430,000, expected to commence in late 2026; plus two unpriced option wells. Noble Viking has secured a one-well contract in Malaysia in direct continuation of existing backlog. Backlog as of April 27, 2026, stands at $7.5 billion. Backlog excludes mobilization and demobilization revenue. Outlook For the full year 2026, previous guidance is maintained for Revenue ($2,800-$3,000 million) and Adjusted EBITDA ($940-$1,020 million), while guidance for capital expenditures is increased to $615-$665 million (previously $590-$640 million) due to the Noble Deliverer’s reactivation. Commenting on Noble’s outlook, Mr. Eifler stated, “With tightening floater fundamentals, the trajectory for dayrates, contract duration and earnings visibility is improving. We continue to anticipate a meaningful financial inflection next year supported by existing backlog and a robust bidding pipeline. Against this backdrop, Noble will continue to prioritize our leading shareholder return program.” Due to the forward-looking nature of Adjusted EBITDA and Capital Expenditures (net of reimbursements), management cannot reliably predict certain of the necessary components of the most directly comparable forward-looking GAAP measure, net income, and capital expenditures, respectively. Accordingly, the Company is unable to present a quantitative reconciliation of such forward-looking non-GAAP financial measure to the most directly comparable forward-looking GAAP financial measure without unreasonable effort. The unavailable information could have a significant effect on Noble’s full year 2026 GAAP financial results. Conference Call Noble will host a conference call related to its first quarter 2026 results on Monday, April 27, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. U.S. Central Time. Interested parties may dial +1 800-715-9871 and refer to conference ID 31391 approximately 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start time. Additionally, a live webcast link will be available on the Investor Relations section of the Company’s website. A webcast replay will be accessible for a limited time following the call. About Noble Corporation plc Noble is a leading offshore drilling contractor for the oil and gas industry. The Company owns and operates one of the most modern, versatile, and technically advanced fleets in the offshore drilling industry. Noble and its predecessors have been engaged in the contract drilling of oil and gas wells since 1921. Noble performs, through its subsidiaries, contract drilling services with a fleet of offshore drilling units focused largely on ultra-deepwater and high specification jackup drilling opportunities in both established and emerging regions worldwide. Generally, a non-GAAP financial measure is a numerical measure of a company’s performance, financial position, or cash flows that excludes or includes amounts that are not normally included or excluded in the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. The Company defines “Adjusted EBITDA” as net income (loss) adjusted for interest expense, net of amounts capitalized; interest income and other, net; income tax benefit (provision); and depreciation and amortization expense, as well as, if applicable, gain (loss) on extinguishment of debt, net; losses on economic impairments; amortization of intangible assets and contract liabilities, net; restructuring and similar charges; costs related to mergers and integrations; and certain other infrequent operational events. We believe that the Adjusted EBITDA measure provides greater transparency of our core operating performance. We prepare Adjusted Net Income (Loss) by eliminating from Net Income (Loss) the impact of a number of non-recurring items we do not consider indicative of our on-going performance. We prepare Adjusted Diluted Earnings (Loss) per Share by eliminating from Diluted Earnings (Loss) per Share the impact of a number of non-recurring items we do not consider indicative of our on-going performance. Similar to Adjusted EBITDA, we believe these measures help identify underlying trends that could otherwise be masked by the effect of the non-recurring items we exclude in the measure. The Company also discloses free cash flow as a non-GAAP liquidity measure. Free cash flow is calculated as Net cash provided by (used in) operating activities less cash paid for capital expenditures. We believe Free Cash Flow is useful to investors because it measures our ability to generate or use cash. Once business needs and obligations are met, this cash can be used to reinvest in the company for future growth or to return to shareholders through dividend payments or share repurchases. We may have certain obligations such as non-discretionary debt service that are not deducted from the measure. Such business needs, obligations, and other non-discretionary expenditures that are not deducted from Free Cash Flow would reduce cash available for other uses including return of capital. We believe that these non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information about our financial performance, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects, and allow for greater transparency with respect to key metrics used by our management team for financial and operational decision-making. We are presenting these non-GAAP financial measures to assist investors in seeing our financial performance through the eyes of management, and because we believe that these measures provide an additional tool for investors to use in comparing our core financial performance over multiple periods with other companies in our industry. These non-GAAP adjusted measures should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, contract drilling revenue, contract drilling costs, contract drilling margin, average daily revenue, operating income, cash flows from operations, or other measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP.
